explanation: Single free-falling body with large dt=1/30 and high speed triggers fast-body substepping (71 substeps reported). Semi-implicit Euler applies gravity each substep while falling, but the effective velocity gain (~6 m/s in 0.033s, i.e. ~180 m/s^2) is ~6x gravity (30). This indicates the substep loop over-integrates gravity / double-counts acceleration for fast bodies, injecting ~315 J in one step with no controller work, breaking energy_bound.
